en.title: Minimum Subsequence Errors with Unknown Binary Bits
en.description:
Replace each ! with 0 or 1; every index pair i<j forming 01 costs x, and every pair forming 10 costs y. First find the minimum total cost, then take it modulo 10⁹+7; do not compare costs after taking the modulus.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains errorString (length 1..100000), and the second line contains x y (0..10⁹).
en.explanation: Example 1: set everything to 0; there are no pairs of different values, cost 0. Example 2: choosing 001 or 011 both produce two 01 pairs, cost 4. Example 3: the only 10 subsequence costs 5.
hints: If x>y, reverse the string and swap the costs. After that x≤y, and there is an optimal solution in which the unknown bits are 0s followed by 1s. Start with all unknown bits set to 1, then change them to 0 one by one from left to right, updating the cost with the counts of 0/1 on the left and right, and take the minimum over all split points.
